title: Park West Management Corp. v. Mitchell
text:
This is a synthetic test fixture, not the real opinion text -- sized to comfortably exceed chunk_case_text's default max_tokens of four hundred words, so that ingesting this fixture through the real normalize-then-chunk-then-index pipeline reliably produces more than one chunk without needing to pass a custom max_tokens value in tests, the same way production code calls chunk_case_text with only text and citation and nothing else.

Paragraph two of the synthetic fixture continues the same pattern, repeating enough words to push the running word count toward and then past the packing threshold that chunk_case_text uses when grouping consecutive paragraphs together into a single chunk before starting a new one, since the whole point of this fixture is to exercise that packing behavior under realistic default settings rather than under a special test-only configuration that production ingestion would never actually use.

Paragraph three keeps going in the same vein, again just filler content meant only to exercise the paragraph-boundary splitting logic rather than to resemble any real judicial reasoning about landlord-tenant law or the implied warranty of habitability, though the real Park West Management Corp. v. Mitchell opinion this fixture stands in for is in fact the case that established that doctrine under New York Real Property Law section two hundred thirty-five-b.

Paragraph four is here so that the fixture comfortably exceeds several chunks' worth of text even at the default max_tokens setting, giving integration tests something concrete to assert chunk counts, chunk boundaries, and per-chunk embedding presence against when they run this fixture through the full upsert_case_document write path against a real Postgres and pgvector instance.

Paragraph five continues padding out the fixture with more filler text, since case-law opinions in production are typically thousands of words long and a synthetic fixture that only produces one chunk would fail to actually exercise the multi-chunk code path this whole feature exists to test in the first place, which would defeat the purpose of having a dedicated case-law fixture at all.

Paragraph six, the final paragraph, closes out the synthetic fixture with a bit more filler text so the overall document is long enough to be split into several chunks reliably across the default max_tokens value used by production code, giving a healthy margin above the four hundred word threshold rather than sitting right at the boundary where a small wording change could flip the test's outcome unexpectedly.

Paragraph seven adds a further, final margin of extra filler words beyond the six paragraphs above, specifically because the fixture landed just under the four hundred word packing threshold once the earlier paragraphs were counted precisely, and a fixture that sits right at a boundary is exactly the kind of fragile test setup this project's own testing conventions try to avoid, so this paragraph exists purely to push the total word count comfortably past that threshold with room to spare.
